text: Call torch.save on the dictionary returned by model.state_dict() to write the learned parameters to disk. A checkpoint that will be used to resume training should also store the optimizer state and the number of finished epochs, not only the model weights.

To restore a model, build the same architecture first, then call model.load_state_dict(torch.load(path)). The call copies tensors into the existing parameters and raises an error when a key is missing or unexpected, unless strict loading is switched off.

Resuming training means loading three things: the model parameters, the optimizer state and the scheduler state, then continuing from the epoch after the last finished one. Seeding the data loader again gives a repeatable order of batches for the epoch that is replayed.

```python
checkpoint = {
    "epoch": epoch,
    "model": model.state_dict(),
    "optimizer": optimizer.state_dict(),
}
torch.save(checkpoint, "last.pt")
```
The loop below is longer than one passage, so it is split at line boundaries into fragments that keep their indentation. Each fragment links back to the complete example.

for epoch in range(start_epoch, num_epochs):
    model.train()
    for batch in train_loader:
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        logits = model(batch["inputs"])
        loss = loss_fn(logits, batch["labels"])
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()

scheduler.step()
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for batch in val_loader:
            logits = model(batch["inputs"])
            val_loss += loss_fn(logits, batch["labels"]).item()

torch.save({"epoch": epoch, "model": model.state_dict(),
                "optimizer": optimizer.state_dict()}, "last.pt")

A model starts in training mode. Call model.eval() before validation so that dropout layers stop dropping units and batch normalization uses its stored running statistics. Call model.train() again before the next training epoch.

Wrap validation in torch.no_grad() to avoid building the autograd graph. Evaluation mode does not disable gradients by itself; the two switches are independent. A parameter with requires_grad set to False is frozen and is skipped by the optimizer.

Gradient accumulation runs several small batches before one optimizer step. Divide each loss by the number of accumulation steps, call backward on every batch, and call optimizer.zero_grad() only after the step. This trades model speed for memory.

AutoModel.from_pretrained(name) downloads the configuration and the weights of a pretrained model and returns a PyTorch module. Call model.save_pretrained(directory) to store both, then load the saved directory later without a network connection.

AutoModelForSequenceClassification adds a classification head on top of the encoder, which is randomly initialized when it is not part of the checkpoint. The head must be trained before its scores are useful.

Load a tokenizer with AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name). The tokenizer turns text into input ids and an attention mask; special tokens such as [CLS] and [SEP] are added around a pair of sentences. A question and a passage can be encoded together as one pair.

Padding makes sequences in a batch the same length, and truncation cuts sequences that are longer than max_length. Pass padding=True and truncation=True to the tokenizer call. A model reads the attention mask to ignore padded positions.
Words that are not in the vocabulary map to the unknown token <unk>, or are split into smaller word pieces. Inspect the result with tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens(ids).
